topic: Capability commitment and source release crosswalk
recommended_candidate: Full platform is directed. Attest exact row-level obligations, duplicates, and optional or conflicting scope. Preserve every required feature in final release.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Choose native or approved integration only where sources permit. Build waves may change implementation order while keeping the final obligations.
closure_evidence: Sign scope ledger and map each enabled capability to approved contract, owner and release.
technical_rationale: Explicit scope prevents registry staging codes or prototype visibility from committing product behavior.
security_implications: Uncommitted actions remain unavailable; scope changes re-open impacted authorization and threat review.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Approve a candidate core journey from install and claim to sign-in, scoped observation, and one safe reconciled mutation. Name exact feature IDs, exclusions and release owner.
source_disposition: Unified console is approved product direction (P1 OD-01 and ADR-020). S0–S4 are source labels.
v4_approval_state: Authorized objective; precise disputed scope pending

topic: Atomic source and runtime UI reconciliation
recommended_candidate: Review atomic text and exercise the existing static prototype in isolation when authorized. Collect versioned state/control evidence.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Static-only intake is reproducible and leaves reachability, handlers and hidden controls unresolved.
closure_evidence: Reviewer attests exhaustive source and rendered-state disposition. This is primarily an evidence closure, with human decisions needed for actual conflicts.
technical_rationale: Atomic source reconciliation and rendered evidence answer different questions; preserve source anchors while testing conditions and transitions.
security_implications: Static visibility cannot establish permission. Use isolated synthetic browser evidence and record denied paths.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Classify each in-scope clause and control; attach exact source/browser revision, actor, selector, state, action and outcome. Escalate actual product conflicts only.
source_disposition: Evidence workflow and attestation, with product approval only for conflicting interpretations.

recommended_candidate: Start with a local authenticated Unix socket, root-owned typed registry and host journal.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Remote agents require mutual authentication, rotation, reachability and a compromised-control-plane model.
closure_evidence: Approve peer IDs, root-owned allowlist, target identity checks, replay and fencing behavior.
technical_rationale: A narrow helper protocol keeps general web parsing and workflow state outside the privileged boundary.
security_implications: Peer checks and root-owned allowlists constrain allowed verbs. A compromised allowed peer can invoke its whole allowlist; host root remains outside tenant isolation.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Freeze per-verb schemas, privilege, stable target proof, fencing, journal outcomes and recovery. Disable remote agent and unobservable automatic retry unless approved.
source_disposition: P1 §§35–36 assigns human authorization to API/dispatcher and host enforcement to helper.

recommended_candidate: Use explicit per-workspace membership, separate ownership edges and default deny at HTTP, jobs and artifacts.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Broader inherited delegation reduces admin effort but enlarges blast radius and needs explicit relationship semantics.
closure_evidence: Approve all grants, revocation boundaries, transfer, last owner and support policy.
technical_rationale: Authoritative owner edges and current grants let scope be recomputed at every access and effect boundary.
security_implications: Deny unknown or foreign scope, stale grants and unauthorized artifacts. Keep support leases explicit, time-limited and auditable.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Approve role/action/resource tuples, transfer revision, revocation during work and streams, last-owner rule and support policy.
source_disposition: Source persona codes and workspace switching do not grant authority.

recommended_candidate: Review an installation-local, purpose-bound, one-use recovery grant that preserves MFA.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Email-only recovery reduces host privilege exposure but leaves users without recovery when delivery is unavailable.
closure_evidence: Approve proof of authority, TTL, session effects, audit, MFA continuity and fallback.
technical_rationale: Single-use local recovery covers delivery failure while preserving normal authentication boundaries.
security_implications: Bind proof, purpose, installation and expiry; consume atomically; revoke old sessions and preserve enrolled MFA. Avoid exposing raw recovery material.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Approve local proof and console flow, no-bypass semantics, recovery alternatives, TTL, audit and safe denial.
source_disposition: Prototype recovery is simulated; source requires no MFA bypass.

recommended_candidate: Keep only secret references in ordinary data. Use scoped broker or envelope encryption with separate key custody.
alternative_and_tradeoff: A fully external vault improves separation and adds availability and bootstrap dependencies.
closure_evidence: Approve secret classes, rotation, revocation, operator access, audit and recovery.
technical_rationale: Stable secret references support rotation and restrict plaintext distribution across panel, helper and workers.
security_implications: Separate custody, scope provider access, redact logs and preserve recovery when key infrastructure is unavailable.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Choose custody per credential class; define rotation, revoke, backup key recovery, incident handling and operator access.
source_disposition: Credential decisions apply to future execution only.

recommended_candidate: Grant future tasks narrow repo/branch and disposable target scope using time-bounded credentials. Separate release approver.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Broader standing access increases potential impact, review burden and recovery exposure.
closure_evidence: Record named owners, target IDs, protected actions, evidence access, expiry and revocation.
technical_rationale: Per-task authority binds access to approved repo, branch, environment, target and operation.
security_implications: Time-bound separate credentials and independent release approval limit unauthorized effects. Documentation approval grants no infrastructure access.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Name authorized scopes, expiry, permitted operations, protected merges, approvers, credential references and revocation.
source_disposition: No repository or VPS authority was provided for this review.

recommended_candidate: Review the unprivileged modular control plane and separate host/build trust boundaries. Qualify the topology for the full platform, including approved multi-node scope.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Use independently deployed services where scaling or isolation warrants them; this adds service identity and recovery complexity.
closure_evidence: Freeze process, transport and privilege boundaries plus minimum supported resource profile.
technical_rationale: Modular single process reduces deployment coordination while retaining a distinct trust boundary for host execution.
security_implications: Keep the web/API process unprivileged; isolate untrusted builds and credential access from helper and control store.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Freeze process placement, IPC, static UI packaging, resource limits and failure domains.
source_disposition: Historic Go/static UI is an inherited direction, not v3.1 adoption.

recommended_candidate: Decide storage using durability, concurrency and restore evidence for all approved topologies. SQLite WAL is a single-host candidate.
alternative_and_tradeoff: External database offers a different scaling/availability model and adds provisioning and recovery dependencies.
closure_evidence: Select engine, migration compatibility matrix, durability settings and restore drill.
technical_rationale: A local transactional store fits single-host intent/outbox atomicity. Verify concurrency and durability before promising limits.
security_implications: Ownership relations and secret references must be enforced transactionally; migration backups need separate custody and restore proof.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Freeze engine, schema constraints/indexes, durability settings, migration order and recovery from interrupted upgrade.

recommended_candidate: Durable transactional jobs and outbox with leases, monotonically fenced effects and observation before replay.
alternative_and_tradeoff: External broker supplies queue tooling but does not by itself solve durable intent or host deduplication.
closure_evidence: Approve retries, lease policy, state transitions, cancel semantics and ambiguity handling.
technical_rationale: Durable intent and transactional outbox avoid losing accepted work. Lease and effect fencing solve separate stale-worker risks.
security_implications: Recheck grants before dispatch; ambiguity blocks unsafe replay. A queue cannot guarantee exactly-once external effects.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Freeze operation states, canonical intent, retry and lease limits, journal interaction, cancellation, observation and terminal CAS.
source_disposition: DB-engine choice and job semantics must be co-designed.

recommended_candidate: Use a versioned namespace with one canonical schema and stable errors; preserve source routes as candidates.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Publishing historic aliases increases compatibility, authorization and deprecation burden.
closure_evidence: Approve route-by-route schema, statuses, idempotency and compatibility.
technical_rationale: A canonical versioned interface prevents historic path aliases from acquiring unreviewed behavior.
security_implications: Check visibility before replay lookup; bind pagination and idempotency to scope. Protect browser mutations and validate callbacks independently.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Approve each selected method/path and request/response/error fixture, compatibility window and disabled route behavior.
source_disposition: Historic route catalog is candidate evidence, not publication.

recommended_candidate: Pick one verified apt/systemd host tuple per initial support tier after install, upgrade and restore proof.
alternative_and_tradeoff: A broad Ubuntu/Debian claim increases ongoing matrix and support cost.
closure_evidence: Name supported releases, architectures, images and exclusions.
technical_rationale: One exact qualified host tuple makes install/upgrade claims reproducible and narrows adapter variation.
security_implications: Unsupported systems fail preflight before mutation. Package rollback and host recovery require distinct evidence.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Name distro release, architecture, image/kernel/init/package backend and verified install/upgrade/restore paths.
source_disposition: Ubuntu/Debian apt/systemd are candidate direction, not an approved matrix.

topic: Web server and runtime support matrix
recommended_candidate: Approve lifecycle and compatibility profiles for every required web and runtime capability. Static hosting is a dependency milestone.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Develop adapters concurrently for earlier integration feedback; this increases compatibility and isolation verification load.
closure_evidence: Publish feature-to-runtime and host eligibility matrix.
technical_rationale: Static hosting limits early runtime/supervisor dependencies; adapter commitments can grow from measured compatibility.
security_implications: Protect unit identities, per-site principals and filesystem roots. Optional CLI, OCI and terminals need explicit privilege review.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Publish feature/version/host eligibility and unavailable behavior; verify isolated workload restart and safe rollback.

topic: Mail transport and optional mailbox hosting
recommended_candidate: Define separate SMTP recovery and mailbox contracts and agree native versus integrated provider coverage.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Use an external mailbox provider where accepted; support, tenant identity, abuse and data custody boundaries change.
closure_evidence: Approve SMTP provider interface, security and failure policies; record mailbox disposition.
technical_rationale: SMTP isolates transactional recovery from mail server operations; acceptance and actual delivery differ.
security_implications: Protect reset material and avoid account enumeration. Reconcile ambiguous send outcomes before retry.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Name adapter, transport/security policy, delivery observability, retries and optional mailbox deferral.
source_disposition: Delivery is unknown without trusted provider evidence.

topic: Backup encryption, retention and restore guarantees
recommended_candidate: Require encrypted independently restorable backups, plus an off-host recoverable copy for disaster recovery where committed.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Local-only snapshots ease operation but cannot survive complete VPS loss.
closure_evidence: Approve consistency class, destinations, key custody, retention, RPO/RTO and cutover rehearsal.
technical_rationale: Independent recovery requires backup integrity plus access to keys and a usable application-level restore.
security_implications: Encrypt and scope backup retrieval and cutover; keep destructive recovery separate from verification. Local copies cannot cover host loss.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Approve consistency, key and retention policy, separate recovery location if in scope, measured RPO/RTO and cutover approval.

recommended_candidate: Require separate domain control proof, DNS target observation and independent HTTPS probe before activation.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Manual certificate/DNS workflow reduces automation and leaves ongoing operator duties.
closure_evidence: Approve proof method, DNS validation rules, certificate issuer/challenge, retries and access fallback.
technical_rationale: DNS control, DNS target alignment and live HTTPS rules catch different activation failures.
security_implications: Prevent hostname takeover and preserve management fallback. Wrong SAN, expiry and wrong target must not become serving-ready.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Approve proof and issuer strategy, validity/renewal, rollback, IPv4/IPv6 checks as applicable and access fallback.
source_disposition: Prototype verification has no live production evidence.

recommended_candidate: Resolve native, integrated or optional status for commercial and portal features while retaining required account and delegation behavior.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Choose native commerce for direct control or an approved integrated ledger/payment path for lower operational burden.
closure_evidence: Record inclusion/exclusion for portal, branding, payments, invoicing, SLA and support.
technical_rationale: Core account provisioning and upstream allocation can operate independently of payments and tax rules.
security_implications: Commercial modules introduce payment callback, refund, sensitive-data and delegation controls.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Record scope of accounts, billing, portal, branding, support and SLA. Show planned versus enforced quotas regardless of commerce.
source_disposition: P2 H-008 requires distinct planned/reserved/measured/enforced semantics.

recommended_candidate: Require exact supported tuples, immutable promotion, verified rollback and named on-call/incident handoff.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Limited pilot support reduces initial breadth but must be stated and enforced as narrower scope.
closure_evidence: Approve supported release channels, environment gates and operational ownership.
technical_rationale: Artifact-bound promotion and support limits prevent evidence from drifting across builds and targets.
security_implications: Require independent promotion authorization, exact-candidate recovery and controls against stale/overbroad approval.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Approve support tiers, incident ownership, staging gate and candidate-bound rollback and approval rules.
source_disposition: Production readiness requires separately executed evidence and authorization.

recommended_candidate: Measure supported workloads and approve a per-environment policy table.
alternative_and_tradeoff: Reusing illustrative test values as service targets creates unsupported commitments.
closure_evidence: Approve values and units for limits, TTLs, rate controls, retention, RPO/RTO, alerting and rollout.
technical_rationale: Measure on named tuples, then set policy; test fixture values are not operating limits.
security_implications: Overbroad leases, stale alerts and lax retention change exposure. Tight limits can reduce availability.
operational_consequences_and_freeze: Approve values and units for TTL, lease/retry, retention, resource limits, rollback thresholds and RPO/RTO. Bind exact policy digest to tests.
source_disposition: No production thresholds are approved by fixture examples.
